vulnerabilities.description: A timing-based side-channel flaw was found in libgcrypt's RSA implementation that may allow a remote attacker to initiate a Bleichenbacher-style attack, which can lead to the decryption of RSA ciphertexts.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase's Java runtime does not use libgcrypt; the package is present only as a transitive dependency of unrelated OS tooling this container never invokes.

ratings.justification: The JVM does not link or call libgcrypt; the package is pulled in only by unrelated GnuPG/apt/systemd tooling this container never invokes, and the base image already ships the fixed version.

analysis.detail: A timing side-channel in libgcrypt's RSA implementation could enable a Bleichenbacher-style decryption attack (the "Marvin Attack"). The container base image currently ships libgcrypt20 1.10.3-2ubuntu0.2, the fixed release (confirmed by pulling the current base image and checking installed package versions directly, since this OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the base image resolves to at build time). Independent of the version, checking the Java runtime's own library linkage shows it does not link libgcrypt at all; the package is pulled in only as a dependency of GnuPG/apt/systemd tooling (gpg, gpgv, gpg-agent, dirmngr, libapt-pkg, libsystemd0), none of which Liquibase invokes. Java uses its own JCE crypto providers, not system libgcrypt.
